utterance: Chloe, your urine test shows signs of a simple bladder infection, and your pregnancy test is negative. You have no fever and no kidney tenderness, so it looks like it hasn't spread to the kidneys. I've prescribed an antibiotic called trimethoprim: one 300 mg tablet at night for 3 days. Finish the whole course. Your symptoms should start getting better within a day or two. You can also take paracetamol for the ache, drink plenty of water, and try urine alkalinisers if they help. Because you're sexually active and don't use condoms, I've also sent a swab or urine test for chlamydia and gonorrhoea. Those infections can cause the same burning, and they often have no other symptoms. The result takes about 2 days and we'll contact you if it's positive. This antibiotic doesn't stop your pill from working, but if you get vomiting or diarrhoea, follow the missed-pill rules. Please come back, or go to the emergency department if it's after hours, if you get a fever or chills, pain in your back or side, vomiting, or blood in your urine, if you feel generally unwell, or if you're not improving after 48 hours or the symptoms come back. If that happens we'll send a urine culture to the lab to choose the right antibiotic. Weeing after sex can help prevent future infections. Does that all make sense?
reply: Yeah, that all makes sense. I'll take the antibiotic and make sure to finish the course. I'll drink more water and try to wee after sex. I'll come back if it doesn't get better or if I get any new symptoms.
